items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and public helpers have docstrings. But reconcileQueryState stacks nested if/else branches for the tie cases with no comments explaining them, and isPersisterRestoreResult relies on `(value as any).__persisterRestore === true`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: persister.ts is a sensible module. reconcileQueryState runs about 95 lines and copy-pastes the five-field error-adoption block three times. A dual marker (Symbol plus __persisterRestore) adds redundancy. Unclear from the truncated patch whether bulk restore shares one helper.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The helper does not normalise or validate the input state (unlike the reference's count/timestamp/fetchStatus normalisation). data and state are both optional, so `{}` is accepted. Defaults like `?? 0` are used, but malformed persisted input gets no validation.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult is exported, and Query intercepts isPersisterRestoreResult(data) before setData; tests confirm onSuccess/onSettled are not called. But the marker is forgeable through the duck-typed `__persisterRestore === true` fallback, and a dedicated reducer action or shared bulk path can't be confirmed from the patch.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Plain-data returns appear to still go through setData, and hidden P2P tests pass 42/42. But the react test needed `persisterFn as any`, which suggests the public type of the QueryPersister/persisterFn signature changed.
